title: Chicken Chow Mein
subtitle: Stir-fried egg noodles with chicken, vegetables, and savoury sauce
excerpt: Chow mein is one of the most popular Chinese takeaway dishes, and it is quick to make at home. The secret is a very hot wok and keeping the ingredients moving so nothing steams.
sourceNotes: Chow mein, meaning 'stir-fried noodles', is a Cantonese dish that became a fixture of Chinese-American and Chinese-British restaurant menus in the 20th century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the noodles and rinse them up to 2 hours ahead. Toss with a little sesame oil to stop them sticking.

content.text: Rinse the cooked noodles under cold water immediately after draining. This stops them cooking further and stops them clumping in the wok.

items.prepNote: cooked according to packet, rinsed cold

content.text: Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat the wok until smoking. Add 2 tablespoons of sunflower oil. Stir-fry the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the wok. Add the garlic and ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the cabbage and carrot. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until just beginning to soften.
Add the noodles and the sauce. Toss everything together over high heat for 2 minutes until the noodles are hot and coated.
Return the chicken to the wok. Add the spring onion. Toss for 1 minute more and serve.

items.symptom: The noodles are sticking in a clump.
items.cause: They were not rinsed after cooking or the wok was not hot enough.
items.fix: Toss with tongs from the start; add a splash of water to loosen.

items.symptom: The vegetables are watery and have made the dish wet.
items.cause: The wok lost heat when the vegetables were added.
items.fix: Add vegetables in two batches so temperature stays high.
